import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [Arrow.arrow]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

def complexity : {n : ℕ} → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → ℕ
| _, ⊤        => 0
| _, ⊥        => 0
| _, rel _ _  => 0
| _, φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| _, ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : complexity (rel r v) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_and (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋏ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_and' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (and φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_or (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋎ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_or' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (or φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_imp (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ➝ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_imp' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (imp φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_all (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : complexity (∀' φ) = φ.complexity + 1 := by exact?

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_statement: For every negative formula φ, the universal closure of φ is also negative.
informal_proof:
First, we consider an arbitrary negative formula φ.
By the property of being a negative formula, we know that all free variables in φ are themselves negative.
Since φ is negative, its universal closure, denoted by (∀x φ), inherits this property, meaning that (∀x φ) is also negative.
Therefore, we have established that if φ is a negative formula, then the universal closure of φ is also negative.

  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [Arrow.arrow]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

def complexity : {n : ℕ} → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → ℕ
| _, ⊤        => 0
| _, ⊥        => 0
| _, rel _ _  => 0
| _, φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| _, ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : complexity (rel r v) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_and (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋏ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_and' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (and φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_or (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋎ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_or' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (or φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_imp (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ➝ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"

  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

| _, ⊥        => 0
| _, rel _ _  => 0
| _, φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| _, ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : complexity (rel r v) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_and (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋏ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_and' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (and φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_or (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋎ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_or' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (or φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
annotation: @[simp] lemma complexity_or' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (or φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

def complexity : {n : ℕ} → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → ℕ
| _, ⊤        => 0
| _, ⊥        => 0
| _, rel _ _  => 0
| _, φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| _, ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [Arrow.arrow]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

def complexity : {n : ℕ} → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → ℕ
| _, ⊤        => 0
| _, ⊥        => 0
| _, rel _ _  => 0
| _, φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| _, ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : complexity (rel r v) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_and (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋏ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_and' (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (and φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_or (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋎ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := by exact?

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"

<STATEMENT>

For any propositions \( a \) and \( b \), the conjunction \( a \land b \) is equivalent to \( b \land a \).

</STATEMENT>
<PROOF>

To establish the equivalence between \( a \land b \) and \( b \land a \), we proceed by considering both directions of the biconditional statement.

First, assume that \( a \land b \) is true. By the definition of logical conjunction, this means both \( a \) and \( b \) are individually true. Since \( b \) and \( a \) are also both true, it follows that \( b \land a \) is true as well. This demonstrates the forward direction of the equivalence.

Conversely, assuming \( b \land a \) is true, we similarly have that both \( b \) and \( a \) are true. Therefore, \( a \land b \) must also hold true. This establishes the reverse direction of the equivalence.

Since both directions have been confirmed, we conclude that \( a \land b \) is indeed equivalent to \( b \land a \).

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_statement: For every pair of propositions φ and ψ, there exists a decision procedure to determine whether φ and ψ are definitionally equal.
informal_proof:
To establish that for every pair of propositions φ and ψ, φ and ψ are either definitionally equal or not, we proceed by examining the structure of the propositions.

1. **Base Cases:**
   - If both φ and ψ are definitionally `true`, then φ = ψ.
   - If both φ and ψ are definitionally `false`, then φ = ψ.
   - If one of φ or ψ is `true` and the other is `false`, then φ ≠ ψ.

2. **Conjunction (φ ⋏ ψ):**
   - If φ = ψ, then φ ⋏ ψ = φ = ψ.
   - If φ ≠ ψ, then φ ⋏ ψ ≠ φ = ψ.

3. **Disjunction (φ ⋎ ψ):**
   - If φ = ψ, then φ ⋎ ψ = φ = ψ.
   - If φ ≠ ψ, then φ ⋎ ψ ≠ φ = ψ.

4. **Implication (φ ➝ ψ):**
   - If φ = ψ, then φ ➝ ψ = φ = ψ.
   - If φ ≠ ψ, then φ ➝ ψ ≠ φ = ψ.

5. **Universal Quantification (φ ➔ ψ):**
   - If φ universally holds for all elements, and ψ is a specific instance of φ, then φ ➔ ψ = φ = ψ.
   - Otherwise, φ ➔ ψ ≠ φ = ψ.

6. **Existential Quantification (∃' φ, ψ):**
   - If there exists an element satisfying φ, and ψ appropriately reflects this, then ∃' φ, ψ = φ = ψ.
   - Otherwise, ∃' φ, ψ ≠ φ = ψ.

By systematically examining each case of φ and ψ, we ensure that for any given pair of propositions, their equality or inequality can be determined definitively. This method provides a comprehensive procedure to resolve the equality of propositions in all possible scenarios.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [Arrow.arrow]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

def complexity : {n : ℕ} → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → ℕ
| _, ⊤        => 0
| _, ⊥        => 0
| _, rel _ _  => 0
| _, φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| _, ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : complexity (rel r v) = 0 := by exact?

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [Arrow.arrow]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma univItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∀^[k] φ = ∀^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, univItr_succ]

@[simp] lemma exItr_inj {k} (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + k)) : ∃^[k] φ = ∃^[k] ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction k <;> simp [*, exItr_succ]

def complexity : {n : ℕ} → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → ℕ
| _, ⊤        => 0
| _, ⊥        => 0
| _, rel _ _  => 0
| _, φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, φ ➝ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| _, ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| _, ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl
annotation: @[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_statement: For every natural number \( n \) and every formula \( \varphi \) of level \( n \), the property \( C(\varphi) \) holds.
informal_proof:
The proof proceeds by induction on the structure of formulas.

**Base Cases:**

1. **True Formula (\( \top \)):**
   - For any formula \( \top \) (true), \( C(\top) \) holds by the given axiom `hVerum`.

2. **False Formula (\( \bot \)):**
   - For any formula \( \bot \) (false), \( C(\bot) \) holds by the given axiom `hFalsum`.

**Inductive Step:**

Assume the inductive hypothesis that for all formulas \( \varphi \) and \( \psi \) of level \( n \), \( C(\varphi) \) and \( C(\psi) \) hold. We need to show that \( C \) holds for formulas formed by combining \( \varphi \) and \( \psi \):

1. **Conjunction (\( \varphi \land \psi \)):**
   - Since \( C(\varphi) \) and \( C(\psi) \) hold, by the axiom `hAnd`, \( C(\varphi \land \psi) \) holds.

2. **Disjunction (\( \varphi \lor \psi \)):**
   - Since \( C(\varphi) \) and \( C(\psi) \) hold, by the axiom `hOr`, \( C(\varphi \lor \psi) \) holds.

3. **Implication (\( \varphi \rightarrow \psi \)):**
   - Since \( C(\varphi) \) and \( C(\psi) \) hold, by the axiom `hImp`, \( C(\varphi \rightarrow \psi) \) holds.

Thus, by induction, for any formula \( \varphi \) at any level \( n \), \( C(\varphi) \) holds.

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or

  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

informal_statement: For any semiformula $\phi$, the complexity of its negation $\lnot\phi$ is exactly one greater than the complexity of $\phi$.
informal_proof: To determine the complexity of $\lnot\phi$, we refer to the definition of negation complexity. By applying this definition, it is evident that the complexity of $\lnot\phi$ is precisely the complexity of $\phi$ plus one.

content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [Arrow.arrow]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

<STATEMENT>

The complexity of a formula obtained by existential quantification is exactly one more than the complexity of the original formula.

</STATEMENT>
<PROOF>

By definition, the complexity function counts certain syntactic features of a formula. When an existential quantifier is added to a formula, it adds exactly one more layer of complexity. Since the complexity of `ex φ` is defined as `φ.complexity + 1`, it directly follows that the complexity increases by one due to the existential quantifier.

  tilde := neg

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

  tilde := neg

  ex := ex

  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by
  simp [Vee.vee]

@[simp] lemma imp_inj {φ₁ φ₂ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n} :
    φ₁ ➝ φ₂ = ψ₁ ➝ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ := by simp [Arrow.arrow]

@[simp] lemma all_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∀' φ = ∀' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [UnivQuantifier.univ]

@[simp] lemma ex_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1)) : ∃' φ = ∃' ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  simp [ExQuantifier.ex]

@[simp] lemma univClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∀* φ = ∀* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, univClosure_succ]

@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]
annotation:
@[simp] lemma exClosure_inj (φ ψ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∃* φ = ∃* ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  /-
    L : LO.FirstOrder.Language
    ξ : Type u_1
    n : Nat
    φ ψ : LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
    ⊢ Iff (Eq (LO.exClosure φ) (LO.exClosure ψ)) (Eq φ ψ)
  -/
                  /-
                    🎉 no goals
                  -/
  induction n <;> simp [*, exClosure_succ]
                  /-
                    🎉 no goals
                  -/

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

Therefore, the complexity of `∀' φ` is strictly one greater than the complexity of `φ`.

The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | rel    {n} : {arity : ℕ} → L.Rel arity → (Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | and    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | or     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"

  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_proof:
First, we recognize that the complexity of an implication is defined based on the complexity of its component formulas. Specifically, for any two formulas φ and ψ, the complexity of the implication `imp φ ψ` is determined by taking the maximum of the complexities of φ and ψ and then adding one to that value. This definition aligns with how complexity is typically measured in logical systems, where each logical connective adds a fixed amount of complexity based on its type and number of components.

The `@simp` attribute in Lean4 indicates that this lemma is a simplification rule, meaning that the complexity of `imp φ ψ` is effectively reduced to the maximum complexity of its components plus one by definition. The tactic `rfl` is used here because the equality to be proven directly matches the definition, requiring no further derivation or calculation.

Thus, by applying this definition, we can conclusively simplify the complexity of any implication in the system to the maximum complexity of its components plus one, which is the core principle we set out to demonstrate.

  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

informal_statement: For any two semiformulas φ and ψ, the complexity of the implication φ → ψ is equal to the maximum of the complexities of φ and ψ, plus one.
informal_proof:
The complexity of an implication φ → ψ is defined to be the maximum complexity of its two components, φ and ψ, plus one. This aligns with the general definition of complexity where an implication introduces an additional layer of complexity, hence the addition of one. 

The proof follows directly from the definition of `complexity` for implications in the formal system, as the Lean4 code (`simp` tactic) applies the relevant simplification lemmas `Semiformula` and `Complexity`. These lemmas confirm that the complexity correctly captures the structure of implications by considering the complexities of the individual formulas and the additional logical operation (implication) involved.

informal_statement: The complexity of the logical OR of two formulas is equal to the maximum of their individual complexities, plus one.
informal_proof: By definition of complexity, the complexity of an OR formula is calculated as the maximum complexity of its two component formulas, plus one. This directly follows from the given definition, confirming that the complexity of `φ ∨ ψ` is indeed `max(φ.complexity, ψ.complexity) + 1`.

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

  | imp    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | all    {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | ex     {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ (n + 1) → Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

abbrev Formulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) := Semiformulaᵢ L ξ 0

abbrev Sentenceᵢ (L : Language) := Formulaᵢ L Empty

abbrev Semisentenceᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L Empty n

abbrev SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (n : ℕ) := Semiformulaᵢ L ℕ n

abbrev SyntacticFormulaᵢ (L : Language) := SyntacticSemiformulaᵢ L 0

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiformulaᵢ

instance : Bot (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨falsum⟩

instance : Arrow (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨imp⟩

abbrev neg (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n := φ ➝ ⊥

instance : LogicalConnective (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) where
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  tilde := neg

lemma neg_def (φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) : ∼φ = φ ➝ ⊥ := rfl

instance : Quantifier (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ) where
  univ := all
  ex := ex

section ToString

variable [∀ k, ToString (L.Func k)] [∀ k, ToString (L.Rel k)] [ToString ξ]

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

instance : Repr (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_statement: The complexity of the disjunction of two propositional formulas is equal to the maximum of their individual complexities plus one.
informal_proof:
Given two propositional formulas \( \varphi \) and \( \psi \), the complexity of their disjunction \( \varphi \lor \psi \) is determined by the following reasoning:
1. The complexity of a propositional formula is defined recursively:
   - The complexity of an atomic formula is 0.
   - The complexity of the negation of a formula is the complexity of the formula plus one.
   - The complexity of a conjunction or disjunction is the maximum of the complexities of the individual formulas plus one.
2. Applying this definition to \( \varphi \lor \psi \):
   - Let the complexity of \( \varphi \) be \( c(\varphi) \).
   - Let the complexity of \( \psi \) be \( c(\psi) \).
   - The complexity of \( \varphi \lor \psi \) is then \( \max(c(\varphi), c(\psi)) + 1 \), as it involves combining \( \varphi \) and \( \psi \) with a disjunction.

Therefore, the complexity of \( \varphi \lor \psi \) is indeed \( \max(\varphi.\text{complexity}, \psi.\text{complexity}) + 1 \).

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic

/-!
# Formulas of intuitionistic first-order logic

This file defines the formulas of first-order logic.

`φ : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n` is a (semi-)formula of language `L` with bounded variables of `Fin n` and free variables of `ξ`.
The quantification is represented by de Bruijn index.

-/

namespace LO.FirstOrder

inductive Semiformulaᵢ (L : Language) (ξ : Type*) : ℕ → Type _ where
  | verum  {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n
  | falsum {n} : Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n

-/

C0_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformulaᵢ.toStr
C0_dependencies.content:
def toStr : ∀ {n}, Semiformulaᵢ L ξ n → String
  | _, ⊤                         => "\\top"
  | _, ⊥                         => "\\bot"
  | _, rel (arity := 0) r _      => "{" ++ toString r ++ "}"
  | _, rel (arity := _ + 1) r v  => "{" ++ toString r ++ "} \\left(" ++ String.vecToStr (fun i => toString (v i)) ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋏ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ⋎ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | _, φ ➝ ψ                     => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\to "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | n, all φ                     => "(\\forall x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ
  | n, ex φ                      => "(\\exists x_{" ++ toString n ++ "}) " ++ toStr φ

informal_statement: For any two semiformulas φ and ψ in the language L, the complexity of their conjunction (that is, φ ∧ ψ) is equal to the maximum of their individual complexities plus one.
informal_proof:
By definition, the complexity of a semiformula is measured based on the number of logical connectives it contains. For the conjunction φ ∧ ψ, where φ and ψ are semiformulas, the complexity is determined by the maximum complexity of φ and ψ, plus one to account for the additional connective "and" introduced in the conjunction.

Therefore, complexity(φ ∧ ψ) = max(complexity(φ), complexity(ψ)) + 1.

This equality holds by the definition of the complexity function for conjunctions, making this a simplification lemma useful in formal reasoning tools.
